questions.prompt: In the Grail story he cites, where does each knight enter the forest?
choices: A At the royal highway marked by the king.
B At the point that looks darkest to him.
C Only after a committee vote on the safest path.
D Never—knights wait for the Grail to arrive.
questions.explain: Each knight goes into the forest at the point that looks darkest to him—entry points that frighten you.

questions.prompt: After voluntary exposure, what does he say people typically become?
choices: A Less afraid of only that one thing, equally afraid of everything else.
B Braver—not merely 'less afraid' of the specific threat.
C More dependent on their therapist forever.
D Immune to all future anxiety without practice.
questions.explain: They don't merely become less afraid of the specific thing; they become braver—there's more to them than they realized.

questions.prompt: What rule of care for the elderly (and therapy) does he endorse about helping?
choices: A Do everything for people so they never struggle.
B Don't do for anyone what they can do themselves—you're stealing from them.
C Help only if they pay cash upfront.
D Never help anyone, ever.
questions.explain: Don't ever do anything for anyone they can do themselves; you're stealing, not helping.

questions.prompt: How does he reframe rules/discipline relative to sophisticated games?
choices: A Rules are only arbitrary control to crush play.
B Rules are enabling principles for more sophisticated games, not mere imposition.
C Rules exist only in sports, never in households.
D Discipline means never allowing any fun.
questions.explain: Rules aren't only something you impose—they're enabling principles for more sophisticated games.

questions.prompt: In the Exodus anecdote about Moses striking the rock, what lesson does he draw for households and negotiation?
choices: A Force always gets you into the Promised Land faster.
B Using compulsion instead of invitation/voluntary assent means you don't reach the destination.
C Deception is preferable to honest offers.
D Silence is the only acceptable leadership style.
questions.explain: Because Moses uses force when invitation was possible, he doesn't enter; likewise compulsion/manipulation blocks household goals.
